question: How can the measurer remain the same despite divisions arising through knowledge?
premises: Divisions appear as inner differences among branches.
The measurer is addressed as present in that same reality.
Knowledge also participates in this division.
inference: Even when divided through knowledge, the measurer remains the same in that very reality.
uncertainties: mātā may emphasize measuring subjectivity rather than a generic knower.
plain_english: Divided by inner differences among many branches, you are still the same measurer in this very reality, even through knowledge.
